metric_rationale: This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Take The Best (TTB) prediction, specifically on trials where TTB and Tallying make conflicting deterministic predictions (i.e., where Tallying does not predict a tie). On these critical trials, TTB will choose the option with the highest validity discriminating cue, whereas Tallying will choose the option that wins on a larger number of lower-validity cues. Consequently, the metric will be near 1 for data generated by TTB and near 0 for data generated by Tallying, providing maximal discrimination.

This metric calculates the proportion of trials where the subject's choice matches the prediction of the Tallying heuristic. The experimental design specifically pits Tallying against Take The Best (TTB) on 6 out of 8 trial types, meaning that under the Tallying theory, this proportion will be high (close to 1), while under TTB, it will be low (close to 0.25). This large mean difference combined with low within-subject variance across 96 trials will powerfully discriminate the two theories.
